raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  # OpenSim 4.6 requires CableSpan via-point APIs merged after Simbody 3.8:
  # https://github.com/simbody/simbody/pull/828
  version: "4.5.2"

package:
  name: opensim
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/archive/refs/tags/${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 53c7c477aeef334109d7ea991251c1f680777d42e59d878fef808ad6d28a98f2
  patches:
    # Use packaged dependencies and Python's active site-packages directory;
    # remove once upstream supports this package-managed layout directly.
    - 0001-use-shared-docopt-and-conda-python-path.patch
    # Backport https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/pull/4103 and
    # https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/pull/4158. Remove with the
    # first OpenSim release that can be packaged and contains both fixes.
    - 0002-backport-modern-spdlog.patch
    # conda-forge's spdlog uses external fmt, so use its configuration-aware
    # wrapper headers. Remove once upstream no longer names bundled fmt headers.
    - 0003-use-spdlog-fmt-wrappers.patch
    # Backport https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/pull/4085;
    # remove with the first packageable release that contains it.
    - 0004-fix-array-bool-linking-on-msvc.patch

build:
  number: 0

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler("c") }}
    - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
    - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
    - cmake >=3.15
    - ninja
    # Match the SWIG version used by upstream's 4.5.x builds.
    - swig >=4.1.1,<4.2
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then:
        - python
        - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
        - numpy
  host:
    - python
    - numpy
    # Simbody 3.8 guards relational operators that conflict with modern fmt;
    # its run export pins the ABI.
    - simbody >=3.8
    # Simbody's public inline API exposes these link requirements to consumers.
    # Build against generic-soname Netlib on Unix while retaining provider-
    # neutral libblas/liblapack run exports.
    - if: unix
      then: libblas * *netlib
    - if: unix
      then: liblapack * *netlib
    # Lower bounds follow versions used by the 4.5.2 dependency superbuild.
    - ezc3d >=1.5.8
    # conda-forge's spdlog links against external fmt, and OpenSim exposes fmt
    # through its public logging headers.
    - fmt
    - spdlog >=1.15.3
    - casadi >=3.6.5
    - docopt.cpp >=0.6.1
  run:
    - python
    # These libraries do not publish run exports, but OpenSim links to them or
    # exposes them in its public CMake interface. spdlog supplies its own.
    - ${{ pin_compatible("docopt.cpp", upper_bound="x.x") }}
    - ${{ pin_compatible("ezc3d", upper_bound="x.x") }}
  run_exports:
    - ${{ pin_subpackage("opensim", upper_bound="x.x") }}

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - opensim
  - files:
      recipe:
        - run_test.py
    requirements:
      run:
        - python
    script:
      - python run_test.py
      - opensim-cmd --version
      - opensim-cmd info Model
      - opensense -H
  - files:
      recipe:
        - test-cmake/CMakeLists.txt
        - test-cmake/main.cpp
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - cmake >=3.15
        - ninja
    script:
      - if: win
        then:
          - cmake %CMAKE_ARGS% -S test-cmake -B test-cmake-build -G Ninja
          - cmake --build test-cmake-build
          - test-cmake-build\opensim_consumer.exe
        else:
          - cmake ${CMAKE_ARGS} -S test-cmake -B test-cmake-build -G Ninja
          - cmake --build test-cmake-build
          - ./test-cmake-build/opensim_consumer

about:
  homepage: https://opensim.stanford.edu/
  repository: https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core
  documentation: https://opensimconfluence.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OpenSim/overview
  summary: Musculoskeletal modeling, simulation, and optimal-control software
  description: |
    OpenSim provides tools for developing musculoskeletal models, simulating
    movement, analyzing motion, and solving optimal-control problems with Moco.
    This package includes its C++ API, command-line interface, Python bindings,
    C3D support, and CasADi/IPOPT-backed Moco solver.
  license: Apache-2.0 AND MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE.txt
    # Lepton has no standalone conda-forge package; its source carries the
    # complete MIT grant and copyright notice.
    - Vendors/lepton/src/Parser.cpp
    - NOTICE

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - jeongseok-meta
